title: Book One · Chapter 86: The Safe Side of the Rail
story:
The class goes to the river on a clear morning.

Miss Wu asked two parents to walk with them. Mum is one of them. She will do one sewing job this afternoon instead. That gives her time to come with them.

Before they leave, Miss Wu checks the names. Every child has a partner. No one may go past the rail. They must not go down the steps to the water.

“We are watching,” she says. “Our model tests stay in the school basin.”

Leo wants to bring his boat anyway. His group leaves it on the shelf. Ronan leaves his at home. They will watch the water, not test models in it. No one needs to lose a boat today.

They walk to a wide place with a firm path. The water is brown near the wall. Further out, the morning sun shines on the moving water. Ronan sees many little patches of light.

Ronan looks for the red sail from his book. There is no red sail today. A low boat is on the far side. A man is working on it. He is too far away to hear the children.

Mei draws the line of the bank. Leo watches a leaf turn near the wall.

“That one is not going anywhere,” he says.

The leaf turns again. Then it moves under another leaf. Ronan begins to count, but there is no clear beginning or end. He makes a curved arrow instead.

Mum stands a little behind the group. A child asks to go down one step for a better view.

“No,” she says. “We agreed on this place. You must stand here.”

The child says he will be careful.

“I believe you want to be. You still stay here.”

Ronan hears her words to the other child. He rests his page on the rail. Both feet stay on the path.

Mei wants to draw the boat across the river. Is the worker standing or kneeling? He is too far away. Mei cannot see his legs.

“Leave the part you cannot see,” Ronan says.

She draws a small dark shape and writes TOO FAR beside it.

Leo finds something different. The leaves near the wall turn in small circles. Further out, a piece of pale wood moves along. It travels down the river. It does not turn back.

“How can the water go two ways?” he asks.

Miss Wu looks with him. She does not give a long answer.

“The water moves differently in different places. We can see both places. Let us record them. I will find a picture about it. We can look at that next lesson.”

On the walk back, Ronan's partner has a sore heel. Ronan slows down. The line behind them grows longer. He does not pull the child along. He tells Mum about the sore heel.

They stop on a dry step away from the road. Mum checks the shoe. Miss Wu keeps the rest of the class together. A folded piece of clean cloth helps until they reach school.

In the classroom, Ronan draws the rail before he draws the river. It takes up a large part of the page.

“Did you see the rail most of all?” Miss Wu asks.

He looks at it. “It was the thing in front of us.”

She lets it stay. Behind the dark line, he adds the two small arrows. The arrows show the two places in the water. The class stood beside this rail to watch. He draws that place too.
studyGuide:
## 重点表达

- rail＝护栏
- bank＝河岸
- further out＝更远的水面
- record＝记录

额外情节词（不要求本章全部记住）：partner＝同行搭档；sore heel＝疼的脚跟；kneeling＝跪着。

## 读句提示

**Is the worker standing or kneeling?**

那个工人／正站着还是跪着？用直接问句表达看不清的问题。

## 理解问题

1. 观察河水时，大人给了哪些明确边界？
2. Mei怎样处理看不清的部分？
